See, i'm split on this issue. Saying "men have the right to void responsibility" isn't a great answer, since that's basically asking "Do you want to pay child support (y/n)." While I agree that child support can screw people over, it also gives the parent with custody the chance to spend more time and resources making sure the child develops under ideal circumstances (good education, food, healthcare .etc). The mother has the chance to abort (if she feels that such a practice is ethically acceptable) to avoid all this, the father doesn't. So, proposal:

Child support, or lack thereof should be determined both by financial need of both parties (no reason someone making 20k annually should be paying child support to a mother making 60k if there's only 1 kid in the picture), custody arrangement (If you insist on seeing your damn kid, and you aren't shouldering any of the load for that kid's survival, that's not okay), and situations involving the pregnancy (did the father ask or bring up the concept of abortion, or adoption, or dropping the infant at a safe harbor location? Did he make it clear that he would leave her over this? If they did, and the mother chooses to keep the child, there is NO reason why the father should be roped in, plain and simple), and those involving the contraceptive (If birth control was used, then the father shouldn't be on the hook for 18 years because the condom broke. If the mother lied and said she was on the pill, then we have bigger questions of dishonesty to deal with here). At the same time, the reverse of all this is true: If the father ends up with primary custody, that mother better be paying up, unless it was made clear that SHE didn't wan't the brat (say the father was poking holes in condoms), but had a moral objection to aborting it.

The current system is BS, but child support DOES still serve a purpose IN SOME SCENARIOS, but it shouldn't be NEARLY as widespread as it is today.
